name: In-between moves
goal: Before you recapture or answer a threat, you can look for a stronger move to play first, such as a check or a bigger threat.
intro: When your opponent captures, the natural reply is to take back at once. Sometimes there is a stronger move to play first: a check, a capture or a threat that has to be answered. This in-between move changes the position in your favour, and you take back afterwards.

parts.title: A capture with check comes first
parts.keyIdea: Before you take back, look for a check or a capture that wins something more first.
parts.text: From a game played on Lichess. You are White. Black has just taken your queen on f4. Before you take it back, look for a move that Black has to answer first.

notes.text: The knight takes the bishop on e7 with check. Black's queen is still there to be taken, and Black has no time to save it, because the king must get out of check first.
Now take back the queen. Taking it straight away would have let Black's knight take yours on d5, and the material would have stayed level. With the check first, you have won a bishop.

parts.title: A check to save your own piece
parts.keyIdea: When both sides have a piece under attack, a check first can save yours before you take theirs.
parts.text: From a game played on Lichess. You are Black. White's rook has just taken a pawn on g7, where your king attacks it. But White's king attacks your rook on h5. The side that moves first decides who wins a rook.

notes.text: The pawn checks the king on g4, so White has no time to take your rook. The king cannot take the pawn on f5, because your rook guards it, and it cannot take the rook on h5, because your king guards h5. So it has to step back.
White's king no longer attacks your rook, so now you take the rook on g7. Taking it first would have let White take your rook on h5.

parts.title: A threat before you take back
parts.keyIdea: An in-between move can be a threat: move a piece with a threat first, then take back.
parts.text: From a game played on Lichess. You are White. Black has just taken a pawn on g4, and your bishop can take back. Before you do, check what Black's bishop on e8 is attacking.

notes.text: The pawn steps away from the bishop's attack and threatens to become a queen on g8. Black has to stop it, and only the bishop can, by going to f7.
Now take back the pawn. Your pawn on g7 is safe, and Black's bishop has to keep guarding g8. If you had taken on g4 straight away, Black's bishop would have taken your pawn on g6.
